title: Tournament time budgets & throughput benchmarking
description:
Two features for running large (24+ player) all-network tournaments:

1. Per-game time budgets for players — forfeit mechanism for slow players that doesn't require engine changes. TimedPlayerWrapper decorator returns EndPhaseDecision on timeout, game continues for other players. Stats tracked and displayed in results so teams know if their players are timing out.

2. Throughput benchmark — measure actual games/hour at various latency × parallelism combinations to determine optimal thread pool size for tournament day.

title: TimedPlayerWrapper with per-call timeout, per-game budget, and stats tracking
description:
## Summary
Create a Player decorator that enforces per-decision timeouts and per-game cumulative time budgets. When a player exceeds their budget, the wrapper auto-forfeits by returning EndPhaseDecision (or first option for forced decisions). Tracks detailed timing stats for reporting.

## Files to create
- src/main/java/edu/brandeis/cosi103a/tournament/player/TimedPlayerWrapper.java
- src/main/java/edu/brandeis/cosi103a/tournament/player/TimingStats.java
- src/test/java/edu/brandeis/cosi103a/tournament/player/TimedPlayerWrapperTest.java

## Implementation

### TimingStats record
```java
public record TimingStats(
    long totalDecisionTimeMs,
    int decisionCount,
    int timeoutCount,
    boolean forfeited,
    Integer decisionAtForfeit  // null if not forfeited
) {}
```

### TimedPlayerWrapper
- Constructor: `TimedPlayerWrapper(Player delegate, Duration perCallTimeout, Duration gameBudget)`
- Follows same decorator pattern as DelayedPlayerWrapper (see tournament/player/DelayedPlayerWrapper.java)
- makeDecision() implementation:
  1. If already forfeited: return forfeit decision immediately (no delegate call)
  2. Otherwise: run delegate.makeDecision() on an executor with Future.get(perCallTimeout)
  3. Track elapsed time in cumulative counter
  4. If per-call timeout (TimeoutException): increment timeoutCount, return forfeit decision
  5. If cumulative time exceeds gameBudget: set forfeited=true, record decisionAtForfeit
  6. On any delegate exception: treat as timeout (return forfeit decision)
- Forfeit decision logic:
  ```java
  options.stream()
      .filter(d -> d instanceof EndPhaseDecision)
      .findFirst()
      .orElse(options.get(0))
  ```
  This means: no actions played, no money played, no buys. For forced decisions (discard/gain/trash from attacks), picks first legal option.
- getObserver(): delegates to wrapped player (events still flow to forfeited player)
- Exposes: isForfeited(), getTimingStats(), getCumulativeTimeMs()

### Tests
- Decision within budget → delegates normally, stats accurate
- Per-call timeout → returns EndPhaseDecision, increments timeoutCount
- Budget exceeded → sets forfeited, all subsequent decisions are instant EndPhase
- Forced decision (no EndPhaseDecision available) → picks first option
- Stats accumulate correctly across multiple decisions
- getObserver() delegates to wrapped player

title: Wire TimedPlayerWrapper into TableExecutor and capture stats in game results
description:
## Summary
Integrate TimedPlayerWrapper into the tournament execution pipeline. All players get wrapped with time budgets. After each game, extract TimingStats from each wrapper and include in the Placement data that gets written to round JSON files.

## Files to modify
- src/main/java/edu/brandeis/cosi103a/tournament/runner/Placement.java — add timingStats field
- src/main/java/edu/brandeis/cosi103a/tournament/runner/TableExecutor.java — wrap players, extract stats
- src/main/java/edu/brandeis/cosi103a/tournament/viewer/TournamentExecutionService.java — pass timeout config
- src/main/resources/application.properties — add timeout config properties

## Implementation

### Placement record change
Add nullable TimingStats field:
```java
public record Placement(
    String playerId,
    int score,
    List<String> deckTypes,
    TimingStats timingStats  // nullable for backward compat
) {
    // Keep existing 2-arg constructor for error cases
    public Placement(String playerId, int score) {
        this(playerId, score, List.of(), null);
    }
}
```

### TableExecutor changes
- Add constructor params: `Duration perCallTimeout, Duration gameBudget`
- In createPlayers(): wrap every player with TimedPlayerWrapper
- After engine.play(): extract TimingStats from each TimedPlayerWrapper via the nameToId mapping
- Attach TimingStats to each Placement

### Config properties
```properties
tournament.per-call-timeout-seconds=5
tournament.game-budget-seconds=30
```

### TournamentExecutionService changes
- Read config values via @Value
- Pass to TableExecutor constructor (or via createTableExecutor() override point)

### Backward compatibility
- TimingStats field is @JsonInclude(NON_NULL) so older round files without timing data still parse
- The 2-arg Placement constructor (used in error paths) passes null for timingStats

title: Display timing stats and forfeit data in web UI
description:
## Summary
Surface per-player timing budget stats in the tournament web UI so teams can see if their players are timing out, how much budget they used, and how many per-call timeouts they hit.

## Files to modify
- src/main/java/edu/brandeis/cosi103a/tournament/tape/TapeBuilder.java — aggregate timing stats per player
- src/main/resources/static/js/playback.js or bar-chart.js — render timing data
- src/main/resources/static/css/tournament.css — styling for timeout indicators

## Implementation

### TapeBuilder changes
Extend tape.json generation to include per-player aggregate timing stats across all games:
- totalForfeits: number of games where player was forfeited
- totalTimeouts: total per-call timeouts across all games
- avgDecisionTimeMs: average decision time across all games
- maxDecisionTimeMs: worst single-game cumulative time

Add to each game entry in the tape: which players (if any) were forfeited in that game.

### Web UI changes
- **Tournament stats panel**: Add a "Timing" section or column showing per-player aggregates (forfeits, avg decision time, total timeouts). Use warning colors for players with forfeits.
- **Playback view**: When a player forfeits in a game, show a visual indicator on their leaderboard entry (e.g., a timeout icon or red badge). This helps during animated playback — viewers can see when a player's rating drops due to forfeit vs genuine loss.
- **Player detail** (if exists): Show timing breakdown — budget used vs budget limit, decisions before forfeit.

### Data format in tape.json
Add to player stats section:
```json
{
  "playerId": "alice",
  "timing": {
    "totalForfeits": 3,
    "totalTimeouts": 7,
    "avgDecisionTimeMs": 145,
    "maxGameDecisionTimeMs": 28500,
    "gamesPlayed": 48
  }
}
```

Add to per-game entries (where applicable):
```json
{
  "forfeitedPlayers": ["alice"]
}
```

title: Throughput benchmark: games/hour at various latency × parallelism
description:
## Summary
Standalone benchmark measuring tournament throughput (games/hour) across a matrix of simulated network latency and thread pool sizes. Answers the question: can we run enough games for a 24-player tournament in 1 hour, and what thread pool size do we need?

## Files to create
- src/test/java/edu/brandeis/cosi103a/tournament/benchmark/ThroughputBenchmark.java

## Implementation

### Setup
- Use the reference engine directly via classpath (EngineLoader with GameEngine.class)
- Use built-in bot players (NaiveBigMoneyPlayer, ActionHeavyPlayer, RandomPlayer) wrapped in DelayedPlayerWrapper
- 4 players per game, random kingdom selection

### Benchmark matrix
Test all combinations of:
- Latency: 5ms, 20ms, 50ms, 100ms (applied via DelayedPlayerWrapper to both makeDecision and observer notifyEvent)
- Thread pool size: 8, 32, 64, 128

For each combination:
- Run 16-32 games in parallel (enough to saturate the thread pool)
- Measure wall-clock time for the batch
- Calculate: seconds/game, games/hour extrapolation

### Output
Print a formatted table:
```
Latency    8 threads    32 threads    64 threads    128 threads
5ms        X g/hr       X g/hr        X g/hr        X g/hr
20ms       X g/hr       X g/hr        X g/hr        X g/hr
50ms       X g/hr       X g/hr        X g/hr        X g/hr
100ms      X g/hr       X g/hr        X g/hr        X g/hr
```

Also report: average decisions per game, average events per game, total HTTP-equivalent calls per game (to validate the ~2,700 estimate).

### Notes
- This is a JUnit test annotated @Disabled (or in a separate profile) so it doesn't run in CI
- The DelayedPlayerWrapper currently only delays makeDecision(). For accurate simulation, observer.notifyEvent() also needs delay — either extend DelayedPlayerWrapper or create a DelayedObserverWrapper.
- If DelayedPlayerWrapper doesn't delay observer calls, the benchmark will undercount event latency. Note this in the output.
